sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Planning Commission Genesis**: Established on **March 15, 1950**, through a cabinet resolution based on the recommendation of the **Advisory Planning Board** chaired by **K.C. Neogy**.
• **Extra-Constitutional Nature**: Neither the Planning Commission nor the National Development Council derived their authority from the Constitution of India or any parliamentary statute; they were **extra-constitutional and non-statutory bodies**.
• **Composition of Planning Commission**: Headed by the **Prime Minister as ex-officio Chairman**, supported by a Deputy Chairman, full-time expert members, and cabinet ministers as part-time members.
• **National Development Council (NDC) Genesis**: Formed on **August 6, 1952**, via another cabinet resolution, following a recommendation by the first Five-Year Plan draft outline to bridge the gap between central planning and state execution.
• **NDC Composition**: Comprised the **Prime Minister (Chairman)**, all Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States, Administrators of Union Territories, and members of the Planning Commission.

items.definition: The formula approved by the NDC in 1969 (and modified later) for distribution of central plan assistance among the states based on criteria like population, per capita income, tax effort, and special problems.

The historical bifurcation of government expenditure created by the Planning Commission, where Plan expenditure related to ongoing Five-Year Plan schemes, and Non-Plan expenditure covered all other expenditures (later scrapped in Union Budget 2017-18).

Descriptive term used by administrative experts (like Santhanam) for the National Development Council due to its overwhelming political authority superseding both Union and State cabinets in economic policy.
A pre-independence committee under K.C. Neogy that recommended the creation of a central planning advisory board, laying the institutional groundwork for the Planning Commission.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Special Category States**: States like Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and North-Eastern states received preferential central assistance (90% grants, 10% loans) under the Gadgil-Mukherjee formula approved by the NDC.
• **Backward Regions Grants Fund (BRGF)**: Designed through planning mechanisms to address regional imbalances in chronically underdeveloped districts.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Rigid central planning, one-size-fits-all approach, lack of state flexibility, and erosion of federal accountability.
• **Policy Interventions**: Replacement by NITI Aayog, introduction of competitive and cooperative federalism, and outcome-based monitoring.

items.title: Mnemonic for Non-Statutory Bodies
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "P-N-N" -> Planning, NDC, NITI.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Planning Commission (1950), NDC (1952), and NITI Aayog (2015) are **Non-statutory, Non-constitutional** bodies.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates traps where options claim these bodies were set up via an Act of Parliament or Constitutional Article.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember the chronological sequence: Advisory Board (1946) -> Planning Commission (March 1950) -> NDC (August 1952) -> NITI Aayog (January 2015).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently includes statements asserting that the Planning Commission or NDC are statutory bodies established under an Act of Parliament or mentioned in the Constitution (e.g., confusing NDC with the Inter-State Council under Article 263). Both PC and NDC were created purely through executive cabinet resolutions.

Mains Value Addition: When analyzing federal fiscal architecture, critique the erstwhile Planning Commission for fostering 'asymmetric centralisation' and contrast it with NITI Aayog's mandate of fostering 'cooperative and competitive federalism' through platforms like Governing Councils.

keyTakeaways: The Planning Commission (1950) and NDC (1952) were extra-constitutional, non-statutory executive bodies that centralized India's developmental planning for over six decades.
The NDC served as the supreme federal forum giving final approval to Five-Year Plans and resource allocation formulas like the Gadgil Formula.
The institutional failure to address localized state needs led to the abolition of the Planning Commission and the establishment of NITI Aayog in 2015.
